label: Level 0
title: Prerequisites
desc: If these feel shaky, system design will feel like magic instead of engineering. Skim, don't linger.

topics.name: Networking Essentials (HTTP, DNS, TCP)
topics.about: How machines find and talk to each other: the request/response model, name resolution, and reliable transport.

topics.name: API Design
topics.about: Designing the interfaces systems expose to each other: verbs, status codes, contracts, and versioning.

topics.name: Data Modeling
topics.about: Shaping your data before you store it: entities, relationships, keys, and the read patterns they serve.

topics.name: SQL vs NoSQL
topics.about: Choosing a storage engine by consistency, flexibility, and the shape of your queries.

label: Level 1
title: System Design Fundamentals
desc: The vocabulary every later topic assumes you already have: how systems talk, scale, and stay up.

topics.name: Client-Server Architecture
topics.about: The workhorse topology: clients make requests, servers respond with results.

topics.name: Scalability
topics.about: Growing capacity without redesigning: add more resources to one box, or split the work across many.

resources.title: Scale From Zero To Millions Of Users

topics.name: Availability
topics.about: The percentage of time a system actually works, achieved with redundancy and failover.

topics.name: Reliability
topics.about: Staying correct under faults; it is about tolerating failures, not avoiding them entirely.

topics.name: Latency, Throughput & Bandwidth
topics.about: Three numbers that define performance: delay per request, work per second, and link capacity.

topics.name: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation
topics.about: Rough arithmetic to sanity-check a design early: QPS, storage, and cache sizes without a calculator.

topics.name: Caching
topics.about: Storing hot data closer to the reader to slash latency and take pressure off the database.

topics.name: Database Indexing
topics.about: Extra lookup structures that turn full table scans into fast point reads.

topics.name: A Framework for System Design Interviews
topics.about: The skeleton every good answer follows: clarify, estimate, design APIs and data, then deep-dive.

resources.title: A Framework For System Design Interviews

label: Level 2
title: Core Distributed-System Concepts
desc: How data spreads across machines, and how those machines agree on what's true.

topics.name: Sharding / Data Partitioning
topics.about: Splitting data across machines so no single node becomes a hot row or a bottleneck.

topics.name: Consistent Hashing
topics.about: A hash ring that keeps key movement minimal when nodes are added or removed.

topics.name: Replication
topics.about: Copying data to multiple nodes so one copy failing is not the whole story ending.

topics.name: CAP Theorem
topics.about: When the network partitions you get to pick consistency or availability, not both.

topics.name: PACELC Theorem
topics.about: CAP extended: even with no partition, you still trade latency against consistency.

topics.name: Quorum
topics.about: A majority of replicas must agree (W+R > N) so reads always see the latest write.

topics.name: Leader & Follower / Leader Election
topics.about: One node writes, many nodes read; election keeps a replacement ready when it dies.

topics.name: Heartbeats
topics.about: Periodic pings that answer the only question that matters: is that node still alive?

topics.name: Checksums
topics.about: Small digests that catch corrupted data while it is in transit or at rest.

topics.name: Bloom Filters
topics.about: A compact 'definitely not / maybe yes' set check that saves a page of disk reads.

topics.name: Message Queues & Kafka
topics.about: Asynchronous hand-off between producers and consumers so services never have to wait on each other.

topics.name: Unique ID Generation
topics.about: Globally unique, often sortable IDs without a single serial sequence as the bottleneck.

resources.title: Design A Unique ID Generator In Distributed Systems

topics.name: Key-Value Stores
topics.about: Simple get/put systems that scale out with partitioning and replication.

topics.name: Rate Limiting
topics.about: Throttling how many requests a client can make per window to protect the system.

topics.name: Long-Polling vs WebSockets vs SSE
topics.about: Three ways to push data server-to-client, each with a different latency and load profile.

resources.title: Long-Polling vs WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events

label: Level 3
title: Architecture Patterns
desc: Recurring shapes that show up across almost every real-world design — learn the pattern once, spot it everywhere.

topics.name: Scaling Reads
topics.about: Replicas, caches, and CDNs: hand more readers the same data without burning your primary.

topics.name: Scaling Writes
topics.about: Partitioning and append-only tricks so writes never collide on a single hot row.

topics.name: Real-time Updates
topics.about: WebSockets, SSE, or polling to keep a page fresh without reloading it.

topics.name: Dealing with Contention
topics.about: Locks, queues, and idempotency for when many users fight over the same resource.

topics.name: Multi-step Processes / Workflows
topics.about: Long operations broken into durable, resumable steps that survive crashes.

topics.name: Managing Long-Running Tasks
topics.about: Offloading heavy work to background workers with progress tracking and retries.

topics.name: Handling Large Blobs
topics.about: Streaming and object storage for files too big for a database row.

topics.name: API Gateway
topics.about: A single front door for auth, routing, throttling, and request aggregation.

topics.name: Redis Deep Dive
topics.about: An in-memory data store pulling duty as cache, queue, and pub/sub bus.

topics.name: Elasticsearch Deep Dive
topics.about: A search engine built on inverted indexes, shards, and near-real-time indexing.

topics.name: Cassandra Deep Dive
topics.about: A write-optimized, decentralized wide-column store with no single point of failure.

topics.name: DynamoDB Deep Dive
topics.about: AWS's managed key-value and document database, built on partition + sort keys.

topics.name: PostgreSQL Deep Dive
topics.about: The relational workhorse: ACID transactions, rich indexes, and a deep extension ecosystem.

topics.name: Flink Deep Dive
topics.about: A stream processor built for event-time analytics across millions of events per second.
